The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that one Nekjan Nessa, mother of the plaintiffs purchased the suit property from Shahjahan Mollah by a registered deed on 23-4-1887 and during the survey operation of cadastral Survey, the property was wrongly recorded and published in the name of her husband namely, Riazuddin under Khatian Nos. 127, 255 and 323. After the death of Riazuddin Sheikh his son namely, Manik Mollah instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 403 of 1916 in the concerned court. One Nekjan Nesa was the defendant No. 7 in the said suit and the entire property of Nekjan Nessa made over to her by compromise decree in the said suit. One Asiruddin purchased the suit property from Nekjannesa by a registered deed dated 10-3-1917. During the survey operation of State Acquisition, the record had been recorded and published in equal share in the name of Asir Uddin and his full brother Tasir Uddin under Khatian No. 337. Tasiruddin had no right, title and interest in the portion of the suit property. Asiruddin had been possessing the entire property. The plaintiffs became the owner by succession after the death of Asiruddin. During the survey operation of revisional survey, the name of Asiruddin had been correctly recorded and published and the successors of Asiruddin had been possessing the suit property peacefully. The descendent of Taseruddin sold out the property to defendant Nos. 1-3 by a registered deed dated 3-12-1995. Thereafter, they had been threatening the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit property and, as such, the plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 2 of 1996 for permanent injunction against the defendant. After receiving the show cause notice of temporary injunction, the defendants erected a Shapra (ছাপড়া) just South West portion of the suit plot and fill up the western portion by cutting earth from the east portion and raised a but on it and, as such, dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit property on 22-1-1996. Hence, the suit for declaration of title and Khan possession of the suit property. 

 9. Mr Md Haroon-ar-Rashid, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below and submits that finding of the appellate court as to possession of the plaintiffs before filling title suit No. 2 of 1996 is not in accordance with law which is not sustainable in law. He submits that both the courts below failed to consider that the plaintiff has admitted the oral gift made by Asir Uddin in favour of Nuru and Hasham. He submits that both the courts below failed to discuss as regard to SA Khatian which were recorded in the name of Asir Uddin and Tasiruddin. In support of his contention he has referred the decision reported in: (1) 4 BLC 349. 

 10. Mr Mohammad Ali Azzam, the learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite-parties opposed the rule and submits that the plaintiffs have proved their case by oral and documentary evidence which were entered into evidence as ext. 1-1ka (deeds of ownership), ext. 2, RS and SA Khatian. He submits that the plaintiffs have proved their case as to possession and dispossession. He submits that trial court observed that suit land is esmali property and without partition suit it is not maintainable. In this contention he submits that there is no evidence on record as to esmali property and the appellate court on assessing the evidence correctly reversed the finding of the trial court. He submits that the learned Judge of the trial court observed that the defendant although claimed the suit property by way of oral gift from Asir Uddin but failed to prove by adducing any oral or documentary evidence against which the defendants also failed to any cross-examination as such defendant is not entitle to get any relief. He lastly submits that there is no misreading and non-consideration of evidence passed by the appellate court and the learned Judge of the appellate court considering the evidence and materials on record rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment of the trial court and he prayed for discharged the rule. In support of his contention he has referred the decisions reported in: (1) 14 BLC (AD) 32, (2) 20 BLT (AD) 173 = 14 BLC (AD) 32. 

 13. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiffs brought a suit for declaration of title and Khas possession. The suit land originally belong to Nekjan Nessa and Nesar Uddin who purchased the suit land by registered deed dated 23-4-1887 which were wrongly recorded in the CS record in the name of her husband Riazuddin. After death of her husband a suit being Title Suit No. 403 of 1916 was filed by her son Manik Molla in the court of 2nd Munsif, Manikgonj where Nekjan Nessa was defendant No.7. The suit was disposed of by amicable Solanama where title of Nekjan Nessa was admitted. Thereafter, Asiruddin purchased the suit land from Nekjan Nessa on 19-3-1917 by registered deed ext. 1ka. It further appears from exts. 3, 3ka SA and RS Khatian 337 that the suit land was recorded in the name of Asir Uddin the present plaintiff opposite-party become the owner and successor of the suit land.
